source_file: Turkishle web vocabulary cards (📝 Kelime Listesi) — headwords missing from the deck (4 candidates dropped after review: already in the deck under a different spelling or inside a combined entry)

items.source: A1-4A vocabulary card (Turkishle web); not in any coursebook list
items.notes: Card only. Filed at A1-4A, the family unit, where its peers (yenge, kuzen, hala) live.

items.source: A1-4C vocabulary card (Turkishle web); not in any coursebook list
items.notes: Card only. Kept despite being a near-cognate: the transparency rule says practise it anyway.

items.source: A1-5B vocabulary card (Turkishle web); not in any coursebook list
items.notes: Tips both ways (issues #55, #57). kalkmak is a vehicle setting off; leaving a person or place is (birinden / bir yerden) ayrılmak, and standing up is ayağa kalkmak — both already in the deck.
items.hint_en_tr: (of a bus, train or plane setting off)

items.source: A1-5B vocabulary card (Turkishle web), carded as “gar / terminal”; not in any coursebook list
items.notes: The card pairs it with gar, which the deck already has as 'train station'. Glossed 'bus terminal' rather than 'terminal' so the two prompts stay distinguishable.

items.source: A1-6A vocabulary card (Turkishle web), carded as “Şehir / İl”; not in any coursebook list
items.notes: The card glosses it 'city', which would collide with şehir, already in the deck. Glossed 'province' — the administrative sense that actually distinguishes it.

items.source: base word of “Van Gölü” (A1-6A vocabulary card, Turkishle web)
items.notes: Base word of the compound the card teaches. deniz and köprü, its peers in that lesson, are already in the deck.

items.source: A2-2C vocabulary card (Turkishle web); not in any coursebook list
items.notes: Set phrase. The deck has gerekli / lazım as adjectives but not this response form.

items.source: A2-2C vocabulary card (Turkishle web); not in any coursebook list
items.notes: Set phrase, carded in the first person as the way the need is expressed. The deck has the noun ihtiyaç already.

items.source: A2-1A vocabulary card (Turkishle web), carded as the imperative “Sağa dön”
items.notes: Carded as an imperative because A2-1A is the imperative lesson; stored as an infinitive to match the rest of the deck. Deck already has dönmek alone ('to return').

items.source: A2-1A vocabulary card (Turkishle web), carded as the imperative “Sola dön”
A2-4B coursebook vocabulary list, carded as “türkü / halk müziği”
items.notes: A türkü is specifically a Turkish/Anatolian folk song, not folk song in general (issue #56). Gloss narrowed to say so.

items.source: A2-4A/4B coursebook dialogues (not in any unit vocabulary list)
items.notes: The second sense split out of “according to / compared to” (issue #47). Same word, so both entries carry a TR->EN hint to say which reading is wanted.

items.source: A2-4B coursebook vocabulary list; also the base word of “halk müziği”
items.notes: Base word of halk müziği, and a list row in its own right. Glossed 'the public' rather than 'people' to avoid colliding with insanlar.

items.source: A1-4C coursebook vocabulary list, glossed there as “to play/steal”
items.notes: New entry so it starts unlearned: this is the sense that needs practice. Its pair, çalmak = to play, keeps the original id and history. Both are transitive.

items.source: gap-fill: in no Turkishle list or card; filed with the A1-3B verbs, where its opposite çekmek is taught
items.notes: Asked about in issue #50 and genuinely absent. çekmek (to pull) is in A1-3B, so its opposite belongs beside it.

items.source: gap-fill: in no Turkishle list or card; filed with the A1-3B verbs
items.notes: Asked about in issue #50 and genuinely absent. Not to be confused with baskın (dominant), which is in the deck and is what prompted the question.

items.source: gap-fill: in no Turkishle list or card; filed with the A2-2C health vocabulary, as karın and bacak are
items.notes: Asked about in issue #50. A list search appeared to find it in A1-4B, but that was Burundi and Yeşil Burun Adaları — the body part is absent. Body parts have no list of their own anywhere in A1/A2.
